gpu_policy.decided: owner, 2026-11-23, before any H GPU work
gpu_policy.reason: cuda5's GPU is shared with another user's training job (yields to other GPU users after ~100 s, restarts ~2 min after they leave) and a batch script of ~1 min GPU jobs (does not yield). In Measurement G, one clear sample followed by our ~35 s CPU start-up let the job return (overlap at 18:09).
gpu_policy.holder: code/gpu_holder.cu, one CUDA context of ours for the whole session; 'work' mode (one 1-block ~1 ms kernel every 100 ms) except while one of our GPU processes runs
gpu_policy.idle_check: 5 consecutive samples 2 s apart with no compute process other than the holder and none of our GPU jobs; otherwise retry every 300 s for up to 12 hours, then stop and report. The holder stays in 'work' through the check.
gpu_policy.per_process: the holder stays in 'work' through the process's CPU start-up (index load) and switches to 'idle' (no GPU work) as soon as a GPU context of ours other than the holder appears, before the warm-up rounds; back to 'work' when the process ends; times in logs/holder-switch.tsv. A process whose context is never seen stops the session.
gpu_policy.overlap: unchanged: 0.5 s poll + pmon during each process; a process that overlaps another user's GPU process is preserved as <tag>-overlap-<n> and rerun, at most 3 replacements per slot (experiments/2026-11-22-range-v3-tune/code/overlap.py; it classifies the holder as ours)
gpu_policy.effects: the holder cannot change our answers (every process is checked against the oracle) and issues no GPU work during the timed rounds; it holds ~150-250 MB; per-process peak memory excludes it; timing is validated against Measurement F's W=4096 cells (cross-session check)
gpu_policy.code: code/session_lib_h.sh (redefines wait_idle and run_slot; the tune session_lib.sh monitors are reused read-only)
